samples.prompt: Write three short anecdotal examples illustrating how unconventional or eccentric behavior can be more persuasive than eloquent rhetoric.
samples.generated:
It was during one of those long and terrible wars which have so often torn this
continent in pieces that I had the opportunity of seeing the power of
eccentricity illustrated by an incident which occurred at a camp-fire. It
was the middle of night, but still the great camp-fire smouldered on in
the midst of the snow. I had fallen into conversation with some soldiers
and we were talking of the great question--How to defeat England? There
was a man in the company who looked like a madman; he had a long black
braid like a mummy's, and the most extraordinary clothes I have ever seen;
a green coat without buttons, and a blue cap made out of a carpet. He
told us he had been fighting all his life; and when I asked him what
had been the result, he replied, "I never lost a battle." "Then," said I,
"if you fight with the Englishman, you must win?" "Yes," said he, "but I
must fight him outside my own country." We were all agreed that this
idea was absurd, and that it would only cost him his life if he tried to
do it. "But why don't you try?" said I. "I am going to!" he answered.
And he went.
